# three_batch_dialogue.jsonl: expected items (written by hand before any parser ran)

The source is one synthetic Codex session, `synthetic-three-batch`, seat `fixture-seat`, client-name list
`["SYNTHETIC-OPERATOR-CLIENT-ALPHA"]` (nothing in it matches). It is generated by `make_three_batch.py`; the digest is
of the exact file bytes.

Batches are the uploader's cut. This fixture is meant to be uploaded as three batches, at the record boundaries marked
in the generator: records 1-3, 4-7 and 8-10 (record 0 is session_meta).

| ordinal | from record | item | detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | u1 | user_text | "Please summarise the plan for the scratch server." |
| 1 | a1 | assistant_text | "The plan: rebase both branches, gate them, then redeploy the scratch server." |
| 2 | p1 | task | step "Rebase", event added |
| 3 | p1 | task | step "Gate", event added |
| 4 | u2 | omitted | omitted_reason "secret" (the private-key marker), no text, no digest |
| - | a2-undated | none | no usable time: skipped, listed in report.json, takes NO ordinal |
| 5 | a3 | assistant_text | "I will not store that key. The rebase is done." |
| 6 | p2 | task | step "Rebase", event completed |
| 7 | u3 | user_text | "Thanks. Continue." |
| 8 | a4 | assistant_text | "The gate passed. The redeploy is next." |
| 9 | p3 | task | step "Gate", event completed |

Ten items, ordinals 0-9 with no gap; one skipped record. The three batches cover ordinals 0-3, 4-6 and 7-9, and each
batch's manifest follows its predecessor's (section 6).

What the acceptance test checks with it: both readers rebuild these ten items in this order with identical keys,
versions and digests; ordinal 4 is an omission whose text never reached the server; nothing from a2-undated is stored.
